Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. An external scalar datum consists of a spin-zero species assigned a mass $m>0$ and elastic two-particle threshold $s=4m^2$. This is a mathematical input package; it does not construct a one-particle scattering state or a scattering matrix. For real on-shell momenta $p_1,p_2$ incoming and $p_3,p_4$ outgoing, with $p_j^2=-m^2$ and $p_1+p_2=p_3+p_4$, define

$$s=-(p_1+p_2)^2,\qquad t=-(p_1-p_3)^2,\qquad u=-(p_1-p_4)^2.$$

Then $s+t+u=4m^2$. The forward slice is the complex-valued function $A(s)=\mathcal A(s,0,4m^2-s)$ obtained by analytically continuing the identical-scalar $2\to2$ amplitude to $t=0$. The crossing action on this slice is $s\mapsto4m^2-s$, which exchanges $s$ and $u$. Assume $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$ wherever both sides are defined.

For context, when a full $t$-dependent amplitude is supplied, use the partial-wave normalization

$$\mathcal A(s,t,u)=16\pi\sqrt{\frac{s}{s-4m^2}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}(2\ell+1)P_\ell\!\left(1+\frac{2t}{s-4m^2}\right)a_\ell(s),\qquad P_\ell(1)=1,$$

where $\ell$ is a nonnegative integer and $P_\ell$ is the Legendre polynomial. The forward result below uses only the optical-theorem sign $\operatorname{Im}A(s+i0)\ge0$ for $s\ge4m^2$; a full partial-wave realization is not inferred from this definition. In the displayed normalization, this sign follows when the forward partial-wave sum converges and the supplied partial waves obey $\operatorname{Im}a_\ell(s)\ge|a_\ell(s)|^2\ge0$.

Put $\nu_0=2m^2$ and $v=s-2m^2$, so $u-2m^2=-v$. Choose finitely many real numbers $p_j\in(0,4m^2)\setminus\{2m^2\}$ and real residues $r_j$, and set

$$P(s)=\sum_j\left(\frac{r_j}{s-p_j}+\frac{r_j}{4m^2-p_j-s}\right).$$

Each summand pair is the real simple-pole principal part at $s=p_j$ and its $s\leftrightarrow u$ crossing partner; hence $P(4m^2-s)=P(s)$. These poles lie off the two-particle cuts. Define the pole-subtracted forward function $B(v)=A(2m^2+v)-P(2m^2+v)$. Assume $B$ is holomorphic on

$$\Omega_{\nu_0}=\mathbb C\setminus\bigl((-\infty,-\nu_0]\cup[\nu_0,\infty)\bigr),$$

real analytic there, meaning $B(\overline v)=\overline{B(v)}$, and has finite upper and lower boundary values on both cuts except at their endpoints. Here the two-particle gap is the open interval $(-\nu_0,\nu_0)$ in the $v$ variable; no massless pole or cut reaches the forward point $t=0$.

Assume the exact high-energy condition $B(w)=o(|w|^2)$ uniformly as $|w|\to\infty$ in the closed upper half-plane, including upper cut-bank limits. In particular this holds on the large upper semicircles after any fixed bounded horizontal translation. For $\nu\ge\nu_0$, define the absorptive density $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}B(\nu+i0)$. Require $\rho$ to be nonnegative and Riemann integrable on every compact subinterval of $[\nu_0,\infty)$, and require $\int_{\nu_0}^{\infty}\rho(\nu)\nu^{-3}\,d\nu$ to converge as a finite improper Riemann integral. For every real $v$ with $|v|<\nu_0$, require the integrals along both sides of the two cuts of $[B(x)-B(0)]/[x^2(x-v)]$, with boundary values taken from the upper and lower half-planes, to exist as finite improper Riemann limits. Require also that the small endpoint arcs at $\pm\nu_0$ for this integrand vanish in the contour limit. Since $P$ is real off its poles, $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}A(2m^2+\nu+i0)$ on the right cut.

The normalized forward Taylor coefficients are $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ for integers $n\ge1$. They have units $(\text{mass})^{-4n}$; $\nu_0$ has units $(\text{mass})^2$. No sign is assigned here to a generic off-shell Lagrangian coefficient.

Let $m>0$, let $A(s)$ be the forward slice of identical-scalar amplitude data satisfying $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$, and let $P(s)$ be a finite sum of isolated simple real pole principal parts in $0<s<4m^2$ and their $s\leftrightarrow u$ crossing partners, satisfying $P(s)=P(4m^2-s)$. Let $a\in\mathbb C$, let $R>0$, and let $f$ be holomorphic on the disc

$$D(a,R)=\{\zeta\in\mathbb C:|\zeta-a|<R\}.$$

If $0<r<R$, $|z-a|<r$, and $\gamma(t)=a+r\exp(it)$ for $0\le t\le2\pi$, then

$$f(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\gamma\frac{f(\zeta)}{\zeta-z}\,d\zeta.$$

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb C$ be holomorphic, and fix $z\in U$. Define

$$g(\zeta)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{f(\zeta)-f(z)}{\zeta-z},&\zeta\ne z,\\[6pt]f'(z),&\zeta=z.\end{cases}$$

Then $g$ is continuous on $U$ and holomorphic on $U\setminus\{z\}$. No holomorphy at the filled point $z$ is asserted.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C$ be open and star-shaped, let $p\in U$, and let $f:U\to\mathbb C$ be continuous and holomorphic on $U\setminus\{p\}$. Then $f$ has a primitive on $U$, and for every closed rectifiable contour $\gamma$ in $U$,

$$\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz=0.$$

A nonempty open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is **star-shaped with respect to** $a\in U$ when

$$a+t(x-a)\in U\qquad\text{for every }x\in U\text{ and }0\le t\le1.$$

The point $a$ is a **star centre**. Every convex open set of [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]] is star-shaped with respect to each of its points. The nonemptiness and the chosen centre are part of the definition.

Let $f$ be Riemann integrable on every compact interval $[a,R]$ with $R>a$. The improper integral over the right-unbounded interval is
$$\int_a^\infty f(x)\,dx:=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_a^R f(x)\,dx,$$
provided this limit exists as a finite real number. In that case the improper integral **converges**; otherwise it diverges. In particular, a limit of $+\infty$ or $-\infty$ is divergence, not convergence to an extended-real value.

If $f$ is Riemann integrable on every $[R,b]$ with $R<b$, define
$$\int_{-\infty}^b f(x)\,dx:=\lim_{R\to-\infty}\int_R^b f(x)\,dx$$
under the same finite-limit convention. All finite integrals use the oriented convention.

If the improper integrals of $f$ and $g$ converge over the same one-ended interval and $r,s\in\mathbb R$, then
$$\int(rf+sg)=r\int f+s\int g.$$
The same formula holds for mixed improper integrals when every singular-end piece of both integrals converges separately.

Let $a < b$ be reals and let $f, g : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable
(The lower and upper Darboux integrals of a bounded $f$ on $[a,b]$ as $\sup_P L(f,P)$ and $\inf_P U(f,P)$, Darboux integrability as their equality, and the notation $\int_a^b f$). Then:

1. **Nonnegativity.** If $f(x) \ge 0$ for every $x \in [a,b]$ then
   $\int_a^b f \ge 0$.
2. **Monotonicity.** If $f(x) \le g(x)$ for every $x \in [a,b]$ then
   $$\int_a^b f \;\le\; \int_a^b g .$$
3. **Two-sided bound.** If $m \le f(x) \le M$ for every $x \in [a,b]$, with
   $m, M$ real, then
   $$m\,(b-a) \;\le\; \int_a^b f \;\le\; M\,(b-a) .$$

**Equality in claim 1 does not force $f$ to vanish.** A nonnegative integrable
function with integral $0$ may be positive at infinitely many points; that is
FALSE: a nonnegative Riemann integrable function on $[a,b]$ with $\int_a^b f = 0$ is identically zero on the previous page's
companion. Under the additional hypothesis of continuity the conclusion does
hold, and that is A continuous $f \ge 0$ on $[a,b]$ with $\int_a^b f = 0$ is identically $0$
below.

**Claim 2 is stated for $a < b$ and is not orientation-invariant.** With the
convention of The integral with oriented limits: $\int_a^a f := 0$ and $\int_b^a f := -\int_a^b f$, $f \le g$ gives
$\int_u^v f \le \int_u^v g$ when $u \le v$ and the reverse inequality when
$u \ge v$, since both sides change sign together.

Suppose $0\le f\le g$ eventually toward a singular end. If the improper integral of $g$ converges there, then the integral of $f$ converges. If instead $|f|\le g$ eventually and $\int g$ converges, then $\int f$ converges absolutely and hence converges.

The same assertions hold separately at $+\infty$, at $-\infty$, and at either finite singular endpoint.

Let $B(v)$ and the positive gap scale $\nu_0$ be the pole-subtracted forward-amplitude data with $B$ even and holomorphic near $v=0$. Fix an integer truncation order $N\ge1$. For $n\ge1$ define the Taylor coefficient $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ and the dimensionless forward on-shell coefficient $b_k=\nu_0^{2k+2}c_{k+1}$ for $0\le k\le N$. Since $v$ and $\nu_0$ have units $(\text{mass})^2$, $c_n$ has units $(\text{mass})^{-4n}$ and $b_k$ is dimensionless. Here “Wilson coefficient” refers only to this normalized on-shell amplitude coordinate; it does not identify a generic coefficient of an off-shell Lagrangian operator basis.

For each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r\le N$, form the quadratic constraint

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j}\ge0\qquad\text{for every }(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^{r+1}.$$

For each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r+1\le N$, form the two additional quadratic constraints

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j+1}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j\bigl(b_{i+j}-b_{i+j+1}\bigr)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^{r+1}.$$

The **finite order-$N$ forward-amplitude bootstrap feasible set** $\mathcal K_N$ is the subset of $\mathbb R^{N+1}$ consisting of vectors $(b_0,\ldots,b_N)$ that satisfy every applicable constraint above. The finite truncated bootstrap problem is to determine whether a supplied coefficient vector belongs to $\mathcal K_N$. Passing this finite test is a necessary condition supplied by forward positivity; it is not defined to be sufficient for the existence of a full amplitude-data package as defined above.

For any gapped identical-scalar forward-amplitude data with $m>0$, gap $\nu_0=2m^2$, an even pole-subtracted function $B$ and nonnegative density $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}B(\nu+i0)$ with finite $\int_{\nu_0}^{\infty}\rho(\nu)\nu^{-3}\,d\nu$, let $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ and $b_k=\nu_0^{2k+2}c_{k+1}$. For every integer $N\ge1$, the vector $(b_0,\ldots,b_N)$ belongs to the finite feasible set $\mathcal K_N$ defined by the following quadratic inequalities: for each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r\le N$ and every $(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^{r+1}$,

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j}\ge0,$$

and for each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r+1\le N$ and every such vector,

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j+1}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j(b_{i+j}-b_{i+j+1})\ge0.$$

These are necessary finite positivity tests on normalized forward on-shell amplitude coordinates. Membership in $\mathcal K_N$ is not asserted to be sufficient for a full amplitude or a physical quantum field theory.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on four-dimensional Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Fix a complex affine algebraic group $G$ with no nontrivial closed normal unipotent subgroup, where unipotent means that every nonzero finite-dimensional rational module has a nonzero fixed vector; this is the reductive hypothesis. Fix a finite set $I$ of field species. For each $i\in I$, fix a finite-dimensional complex $\mathbb Z/2$-graded vector space $\Phi_i=\Phi_i^{\bar 0}\oplus\Phi_i^{\bar 1}$, a field parity, and an algebraic representation $\rho_i:G\to\operatorname{GL}(\Phi_i)$. Include the declared spacetime-index action in $G$ or in its specified finite-dimensional representation data. A field configuration assigns smooth component functions on $M$ to the even generators and formal odd Grassmann generators with smooth coefficient functions to the odd generators.

Fix a derivative cutoff $r\geq0$, a maximum polynomial field degree $q\geq0$, and a rational engineering weight $\Delta_i$ for each field species. A derivative $\partial_\mu$ has engineering weight one, and an $s$-jet generator is a component of $\partial_{\mu_1}\cdots\partial_{\mu_s}\phi_i(x)$ for $0\leq s\leq r$. If covariant derivatives are used, their finite jet generators and $G$-action are included explicitly in the same data. Let $J_r$ be the resulting finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z/2$-graded vector space with its specified algebraic representation $\rho_r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(J_r)$. Its polynomial algebra is the supercommutative algebra $P_r=\operatorname{Sym}(J_{r,\bar 0}^{*})\otimes\Lambda(J_{r,\bar 1}^{*})$: even generators commute and odd generators anticommute. For a fixed weight $D\in\mathbb Q$, let $P_{r,q,D}$ be the complex span of monomials of total engineering weight $D$ and total polynomial degree at most $q$.

A local operator in this finite-order data is an element of $P_{r,q,D}$ evaluated at $x$ on the $r$-jet of the fields. A scalar operator invariant under the declared symmetries is an element of $V_{r,q,D}=P_{r,q,D}^{G}$. Engineering dimension means this assigned mass weight; it is not a statement about an observed quantity. In four dimensions a term with operator $\mathcal O_D$ has the convention $C\mathcal O_D/\Lambda^{D-4}$, where $\Lambda$ has mass dimension one and $C$ is dimensionless. Reality conditions, when required for a real action, are additional conjugation data on $V_{r,q,D}$.

Fix a finite jet order $r$, maximum polynomial field degree $q$, engineering weight $D$, finite field-species list, coefficient field $\mathbb C$, and complex reductive affine algebraic group $G$ with the finite-dimensional rational action specified on the jet generators, including the declared spacetime-index symmetries. Let $W_D$ be the finite-dimensional space of all local polynomials of weight $D$ and degree at most $q$, before imposing $G$-invariance, and let $V_D=W_D^G$ be its invariant scalar subspace. An admitted raw relation space is a specified $G$-stable linear subspace $\widetilde R_D\leq W_D$, given by explicit linear identities among the chosen polynomials. Its invariant part is $R_D=\widetilde R_D\cap V_D$. Any action, boundary, or observable interpretation of the selected identities is extra mathematical data and must be stated with the result that verifies it.

The finite-order invariant operator-basis quotient is

$$
\mathcal Q_D:=V_D/R_D.
$$

Two invariant operators represent the same class exactly when their difference lies in $R_D$. An operator basis is any finite list of representatives in $V_D$ of a vector-space basis of $\mathcal Q_D$. The quotient records precisely the declared relation space; it does not assert that every relation relevant to an arbitrary EFT, observable, or infinite operator tower has been included.

derivations.claim: Finite polarization and on-shell contraction define a presentation-independent polynomial; actual forward real momenta verify identities.
Divergence insertions have total-momentum factors and free EOM insertions have on-shell factors, so the certified relations vanish.
Permutation symmetry gives evenness; even derivative number gives reality.
Annihilation of the actual intersection of relations gives descent to its exact quotient image.
Eight assignments for each pairing yield tO8=8m^4+4v^2 and the correctly normalized vector.

boundaries.evidence: The declared relation span can be empty; step 2.2 still defines descent.
The zero operator maps to the zero polynomial by step 1.1; higher O8 coordinates vanish by 3.1.
Exactly one contact insertion is treated, with all four polarizations computed in step 3.1.

boundaries.reason: m and Lambda are strictly positive; no zero-gap limit is asserted.
The map is polynomial and has no analytic cut-boundary limit; full-amplitude endpoint assumptions belong to the dispersion theorem.
